items.title: Percy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Milt had gone, Milt was gone and he was playing with Woody Herman at the time ‘cause Dizzy wasn’t paying any money, so we had to get out of there.

ctx.x: Yeah, right! That’s the date with Dizzy. I was so disillusioned playing with Dizzy, and he would spend ten to fifteen minutes fooling around with that, we used to call it “the barrel,” that conga drum he used to play that Chano had given him. And comedy and what not, and all this scat singing, and we wanted to hear Dizzy play his trumpet, and [we’d] say, “Aww, why he’s fooling around the whole set, he played two songs on the trumpet!” Anyhow, when Percy was born, I was driving one car, me and Dizzy and some of…
So, you first met Monte Kay in 1951?
